text:
maria_cs: Hey team — quick heads up: onboarding run with VelvetForms showed p95 generation latency jumping from 280ms -> 1.6s during peak token bursts. Customer is on trial and renewal conversation in two weeks, flagged as medium risk if we don't stabilize latency.

aj_eng: ugh, do we have the p50/p95/p99 numbers + model & config?

maria_cs: p50=120ms, p95=1.6s, p99=2.8s. Model: redwood/rlhf-chat-13b (default fp16). Batch size avg 4, tokens per req ~ 420. Route currently: hosted-us-west -> standard tier.

kai_research: likely KV cache churn + batching hitting long sequences. Quick wins: 1) suggest int8 quantized variant for warm paths 2) add prefix KV caching for frequent prompts 3) route high-traffic tenant to dedicated pool (or lower-batch, high-SLO pool).

aj_eng: agree. Can we propose a safe canary change: quantized model with fallback to fp16 + route 20% of traffic to dedicated nodepool? If latency improves, shift 80% after 24h.

kai_research: yes. Proposed policy snippet for routing canary (we can paste to Console):
```json
{
  "match": {"customer_id":"velvetforms"},
  "strategy": [
    {"weight":20, "target":"dedicated-usw-llm-q-int8"},
    {"weight":80, "target":"hosted-usw-rlhf-13b-fp16"}
  ]
}
```

sam_support: Customer-facing note: VelvetForms cares about exact wording on hallucination risk with quantization. They asked for a short doc explaining tradeoffs. Can someone draft a 1-2 paragraph blurb I can send before we flip traffic?

maria_cs: I can draft. Will include: expected latency improvements, typical accuracy hit (<=2% on our eval set for this workload), fallback behavior, and rollback plan.

aj_eng: also add an instrumentation checklist for the call: 1) enable debug metrics for token-level latency 2) set alert if p95 > 1s for 15m 3) confirm canary rollback job.

deploy-bot: deploy-plan created: canary policy velvetforms-canary-3965432100 queued. CI checks: ✅, infra quota check: ✅. ETA to apply: 12:10 PDT.

maria_cs: thanks. I'll schedule an enablement touchpoint with product and the customer for 12:30 PDT, send the blurb, and monitor the thread. If we see >5% error rate or semantic regressions on eval set, we'll roll back immediately. :thumbsup:
